craft_notes: Sthāyin: Wonder at all-containing, marveled into refuge. End-dash→comma (straitening softens, lifting lands). Rejected: 'mind him' for 'call to mind' — L3 kept. Read aloud: lands on close.

lines: Mid straits though straitened, slimed with folly's spate,
call him to mind, and wits grow pellucid: Śiva we lift.
l4.sanskrit_cite: mahatsv apy arthakṛcchreṣu mohaughamalinīkṛtāḥ smṛte yasmin prasīdanti matayas taṃ śivaṃ stumaḥ

reads_against.argmap: Even in great hard straits, dirtied by delusion-flood. → Remembrance of Śiva clears deluded minds.
c1_essence: Lone unbroken sway unfolding fall and rise; filth aimed turns sterling.

l2.plain_english: Sunk in dire straits, muddied by floods of folly — let him be recalled, and minds grow lucid: Śiva we sing.
l2.sanskrit_cite: mahatsv apy arthakṛcchreṣu mohaughamalinīkṛtāḥ smṛte yasmin prasīdanti matayas taṃ śivaṃ stumaḥ

reads_against.t1: Even in great hard straits, dirtied by delusion-flood — when he is remembered, minds clear: that Śiva we praise.
